author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be opened showing the date and description it currently holds, and either can be changed. The correction is validated like a booking and replaces the visit in place; the pet gains no second visit. On acceptance the owner's record is shown.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit for correction shows that visit's current date and description, ready to change.
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that visit; the pet gains no further visit.
An accepted correction ends on the owner's record.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the visit is left as it was.
A date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the visit is left as it was.
Correcting a visit whose pet does not belong to the named owner, or that does not belong to the named pet, is refused.
non_goals: Cancelling or withdrawing a booked visit — NG-5 still covers it.
A link or button to the correction anywhere in the owner's record; it is reached by addressing the visit directly.
Any record of what the visit said before the correction: no history, attribution, or audit trail.
Moving a visit to a different pet or owner; only the date and the description change.
notes: NG-5 narrowed per the owner's decision; recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-correction.md and the narrowed Non-Goals row. That ADR needs an index row in docs/adr/README.md, which is outside the product expert's write scope — system-design-expert to add it. Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than raised as consultations, per the dispatch: whether the owner's record should later offer an entry point, and whether a correction should keep what the visit said before. Both take the narrowest reading for this slice: no entry point, no history.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the create/edit twin PetController already runs, applied to the visit in the same owner feature package. Nothing new: same route shape (/edit under the aggregate path), same server-rendered form, same write path through OwnerRepository (system-design.md Contracts, 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'). One adjustment carries it: VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") gains an optional visitId path variable, exactly as PetController.findPet takes an optional petId — absent, it builds a new Visit and adds it to the pet; present, it returns the pet's existing visit and adds nothing, which is what keeps the pet from gaining a second visit. Binding then mutates that loaded instance in the owner graph, and owners.save(owner) cascades an update rather than an insert. Second adjustment: the non-future-date rule moves out of processNewVisitForm into a VisitValidator, the Form validator pattern already in force for pets. architecture-principles.md is explicit that a rule added to a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the existing deviation, so the correction handler must not carry a second copy of the check; the catalog's Form validator row is the sanctioned home and needs no ADR. Create-path behavior is preserved exactly: same field, same error code typeMismatch.visitDate. Aggregate navigation stays through the root — Owner.getPet(id) then a new Pet.getVisit(id) mirroring it — so an owner/pet/visit mismatch cannot resolve.
integration_points: Two routes added to VisitController: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. Both are unauthenticated like every existing route; no management or actuator surface changes.
@ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit serves both route pairs via @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId. It must not call pet.addVisit when visitId is present.
Pet gains a by-identity visit lookup mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer): returns the visit or null, leaving the refusal to the caller.
Write path unchanged: this.owners.save(owner) cascades the in-place update to the existing visit row. No VisitRepository, no new persistence type, no schema change.
Template reused as-is: the form carries no th:action, so it posts to whichever URL rendered it, and the heading already drops the 'New' prefix for a persisted visit.
VisitValidator registered from @InitBinder via addValidators, so bean validation on Visit.description still runs; the controller's inline date check is removed from processNewVisitForm.

patterns.description: findPet: optional path variable on the model-attribute method distinguishes create from edit — the shape loadPetWithVisit takes
initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm: the /edit route pair, redirect to the owner detail page on success, same view on validation failure
Form validator pattern in force (architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog): stateless field-level rejection for a rule the type's own constraints cannot express
getPet(Integer): by-identity navigation inside the aggregate, returning null when absent — the model for Pet.getVisit(Integer)
the non-future-date check being extracted; its field and error code (typeMismatch.visitDate) must survive the move unchanged

risks.risk: Registering VisitValidator with dataBinder.setValidator replaces bean validation, dropping @NotBlank on Visit.description and breaking the blank-description criterion on both routes
risks.mitigation: Use addValidators, not setValidator. PetValidator uses setValidator because it re-checks the required fields itself; VisitValidator does not

risks.risk: The correction handler adds a second visit to the pet, breaching the 'no further visit' criterion
risks.mitigation: pet.addVisit is called only on the create path. Assert the pet's visit count is unchanged on the saved owner in the correction test

risks.risk: A rejected correction leaves the visit changed. Binding mutates the loaded entity before validation runs
risks.mitigation: Return the form view on result.hasErrors() before any repository call. The owner graph is detached (spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled), so an unsaved mutation is discarded at request end

risks.risk: A new message key for a correction-specific heading or button fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest, which requires every base key in all non-en bundles
risks.mitigation: Leave the template's message keys as they are; no acceptance criterion depends on the button text. Adding a key means editing nine further bundles

risks.risk: The error page renders exception messages, so a message for an unresolvable visit could leak internals
risks.mitigation: Mirror the existing owner/pet IllegalArgumentException wording: identifiers only, no query, path, or configuration detail (security-principles.md, secret-disclosure row)

risks.risk: Identifier tampering: a correction addressed at another owner's visit
risks.mitigation: Resolve owner then pet then visit by identity, refusing at the first miss, and keep setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") so the visit identity cannot be rebound from the form

notes: Durable memory updated: docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for 2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-correction.md (the product expert's hand-off item — the ADR itself is theirs and is unchanged); docs/system-design.md Contracts gains a VisitValidator row and REQ-VISITEDIT-001 on the VisitController, Pet, and Visit rows, plus one sentence on how VisitValidator is registered. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is skipped. BRIEF DIVERGENCE for the owner of docs/architecture-principles.md (outside my write scope): its Pattern Catalog note names 'non-future-visit-date' among the checks living in controller methods; once VisitValidator lands, that clause is stale and only the duplicate-name and future-birth-date checks remain. Open questions recorded rather than raised, per the dispatch: (1) the corrected visit appears in the form's own 'Previous Visits' table, since it is persisted and the table filters only unsaved visits — the PRD is silent, narrowest reading leaves it; (2) an unresolvable visit identifier is refused the way an unresolvable owner or pet already is, an IllegalArgumentException reaching the error page — a 404 flow would be a new pattern for the whole feature package and is out of this slice; (3) no flash message accompanies a successful correction — the booking path's flash text is hard-coded English, and a second one widens the REQ-LANG-002 gap while no criterion asks for it; (4) the visible entry point stays out per the owner's decision, so the routes are reachable by URL alone. Method naming: the PRD word is correction, so initVisitCorrectionForm/processVisitCorrectionForm; 'Booking' stays out of new names per ubiquitous-language.md. Coverage basis: no IntelliJ MCP oracle is connected in this dispatch, so every claim above rests on direct reads of the named source files rather than symbol resolution — the weaker basis.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description:
loadPetWithVisit's Javadoc was directly edited by this change (a new

paragraph was inserted) but was not brought up to date with the method it now describes: the signature gained a `visitId` parameter with no matching `@param visitId`, and `@return Pet` still names the wrong type — the method returns `Visit`. A reader relying on the Javadoc alone (the next reader with none of today's context) is misled about both the return type and the meaning of the new parameter.
findings.fix: Add `@param visitId` documenting the absent/present distinction already explained in prose, and correct `@return Pet` to `@return Visit`.

approved_aspects: Pet.getVisit mirrors Owner.getPet's existing loop-based lookup pattern exactly (verified by reading Owner.java:117-127), keeping style consistent rather than introducing a stream-based lookup that would stand out as a one-off.

VisitValidator is a clean, minimal Validator mirroring PetValidator's shape and Javadoc style (verified against PetValidator.java), registered via addValidators (not setValidator) so bean validation on Visit.description keeps running alongside it.

The extracted VIEWS_VISIT_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM constant removes the view-name string duplication the new /edit routes would otherwise have introduced, following the same pattern PetController already uses for its own view constant.

Error handling for owner/pet/visit mismatch is consistent: same IllegalArgumentException shape and message style as the existing owner/pet lookup, so identifier tampering across the aggregate is refused uniformly and no new error-handling pattern is introduced.
No stray logging, no swallowed exceptions, no magic strings duplicated between VisitController and VisitValidator (the typeMismatch.visitDate literal now lives in exactly one place).

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: testing-principles.md § Factory Methods requires new test construction added by a touched test to go behind a factory method, not a raw constructor. `init()` is modified this slice to add `this.bookedVisit = new Visit(); this.bookedVisit.setId(...); this.bookedVisit.setDate(...); this.bookedVisit.setDescription(...); this.pet.addVisit(this.bookedVisit);` — a raw constructor plus four setter calls. The same slice's `VisitValidatorTests.visitOn(LocalDate)` already demonstrates the pattern this file should follow.
findings.fix: Add a private factory, e.g. `private Visit createVisit(Integer id, LocalDate date, String description)` (or an anonymous-factory variant per the brief's Anonymous Factories section), and construct `bookedVisit` through it in `init()`.

approved_aspects: All five PRD acceptance-criteria test names (test_names in the prd-entry) are present verbatim and pass: theVisitCorrectionFormShouldShowTheVisitsCurrentDateAndDescription, theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheVisitWithoutAddingAnother, theVisitCorrectionShouldEndOnTheOwnerRecord, theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheDescriptionIsBlank, theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheDateIsNotInTheFuture.

PRD edge case 3 (visit/pet/owner mismatch) is covered by theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenThePetIsNotTheNamedOwners and theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotTheNamedPets, exercising the shared loadPetWithVisit resolution path with assertThatThrownBy on the real IllegalArgumentException.

Identifier-tampering risk from the design-block is covered directly: theVisitCorrectionShouldNotLetTheFormReassignTheVisitsIdentity posts a spoofed id param and asserts the bound entity's real id is unchanged.

VisitValidatorTests is a genuine unit test — no Spring context, no mocks, real Visit and BeanPropertyBindingResult objects — which measurably improves the project's test-pyramid shape per testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid ('a rule lifted into a unit... adds a unit test').

never().save() verifications on the two refusal tests are the correct way to assert non-persistence given a mocked OwnerRepository and a detached owner graph; they are not restating a behavioral assertion already made elsewhere in those tests.

All new test data (TEST_BOOKED_VISIT_ID, VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET, PET_ID_OF_ANOTHER_OWNER, BOOKED_DATE/DESCRIPTION, CORRECTED_DATE/DESCRIPTION) is named by role with zero bare-literal mystery values, and CORRECTED_DATE/BOOKED_DATE are derived from LocalDate.now() rather than hard-coded.
Test method names in both files follow the brief's the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school.
./gradlew test on VisitControllerTests and VisitValidatorTests is green.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Defense in depth, worth an inline note rather than a change: processVisitCorrectionForm binds submitted values onto the Visit instance loaded from the owner aggregate before validation runs, and relies on the refused correction dying with the request. That holds only because spring.jpa.open-in-view=false in src/main/resources/application.properties leaves the graph detached. The existing comment says 'the owner graph is detached' without naming what makes it so. Since this is a demonstration application that gets copied, naming the open-in-view setting in that comment would stop a reader from lifting the pattern into an OSIV-enabled context, where binding onto a managed entity would flush unvalidated data.

Refused corrections re-render the form with the mutated aggregate still in the model, so the 'Previous Visits' table shows the rejected date/description as though recorded. No persistence occurs and no trust boundary is crossed; noted only because it can read as if an invalid correction took effect.

Supply chain: no NVD match ran in this review. The OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins present: java, checkstyle, jacoco, org.springframework.boot 4.1.0, io.spring.dependency-management, graalvm native, cyclonedx.bom, javaformat, nohttp), and this reviewer has no network access. The change adds no dependency and does not touch build.gradle, so the resolved set is unchanged from the last verified state; Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Jackson version remain unverified against the NVD here and should be closed by CI or a human. The cyclonedx SBOM task and the nohttp plain-HTTP check are both still wired in.
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the class-level unnamed @InitBinder in VisitController (setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")) still applies to every model attribute on the two new routes, including "visit" and "owner". The new @InitBinder("visit") adds a validator only; Spring invokes every @InitBinder whose value is empty or matches the attribute name, so the disallow list is not displaced. Verified by reading VisitController in full and comparing against PetController's named binders. Visit exposes only date and description, so nothing beyond the two corrected fields is bindable.

Insecure direct object reference: the correction re-resolves the whole chain per request (owners.findById -> Owner.getPet(petId) -> new Pet.getVisit(visitId)), each step by identity from the aggregate root, so a visit belonging to another pet or a pet belonging to another owner cannot resolve. This satisfies the 'Trusting cross-request state' row of docs/security-principles.md; nothing is carried across requests.
Pet.getVisit uses Objects.equals on boxed ids and skips new (unsaved) visits, so a null id cannot collide with a null path variable.

Error disclosure: the new IllegalArgumentException message carries only int/Integer path variables (visitId, petId), which the framework has already type-converted, so no attacker-controlled string reaches the error page. Message shape matches the pre-existing owner/pet not-found throws in the same method (security-principles.md 'Secret disclosure through logs and errors').

No new template output: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged, renders every value through th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping on, and its form carries no action attribute so it posts back to the current URL. No XSS surface added.

Data access: no query text is built from request-derived values; the write path stays OwnerRepository.save on the aggregate root. Detection-pattern grep across src/main/java/.../owner/ for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec/FileWriter/FileOutputStream//tmp//nativeQuery returned nothing but the pre-existing @Query in PetTypeRepository (a static JPQL literal).

Concurrency: VisitController remains a singleton whose only field is the final repository; VisitValidator is stateless and instantiated per data binder, matching PetValidator. Type safety: the (Visit) cast in VisitValidator.validate is guarded by supports(), the same shape PetValidator uses.

Exposed surface: the two new routes are documented in docs/system-design.md (VisitController and VisitValidator contract rows, and the Security Context input list now naming visit identifiers), meeting the 'Widening the exposed surface' row. No management endpoint, dependency, or credential is touched; build.gradle is not in the change set.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be opened showing the date and description it currently holds, and either can be changed. The correction is validated like a booking and replaces the visit in place; the pet gains no second visit. On acceptance the owner's record is shown.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit for correction shows that visit's current date and description, ready to change.
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that visit; the pet gains no further visit.
An accepted correction ends on the owner's record.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the visit is left as it was.
A date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the visit is left as it was.
Correcting a visit whose pet does not belong to the named owner, or that does not belong to the named pet, is refused.
non_goals: Cancelling or withdrawing a booked visit — NG-5 still covers it.
A link or button to the correction anywhere in the owner's record; it is reached by addressing the visit directly.
Any record of what the visit said before the correction: no history, attribution, or audit trail.
Moving a visit to a different pet or owner; only the date and the description change.
